jp: 母[はは]は料理[りょうり]が好[す]きだから、{きっと|av-kitto}今夜[こんや]も何[なに]か作[つく]るでしょう。
en: Mother loves cooking, so she will surely make something again tonight.
why: A confident guess that ends in でしょう is opened by きっと.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は朝[あさ]に弱[よわ]いので、{めったに|av-mettani}早[はや]く起[お]きません。
en: My little brother is bad in the mornings, so he hardly ever gets up early.
why: めったに with a negative verb means 'hardly ever'.

jp: 父[ちち]は{全然[ぜんぜん]/ちっとも|av-zenzen}料理[りょうり]をしません。
en: My father doesn't cook at all.
why: 全然 (or ちっとも) with a negative verb means 'not at all'.

jp: {せっかく|av-sekkaku}掃除[そうじ]したのに、子供[こども]がすぐ散[ち]らかした。
en: I went to the trouble of cleaning, but the kids made a mess right away.
why: せっかく ... のに: an effort that was spoiled.

jp: せっかく作[つく]った{のに|av-sekkaku}、誰[だれ]も食[た]べてくれなかった。
en: Even though I went to the trouble of making it, nobody ate it.
why: せっかく plus a disappointing result takes のに.

jp: {まさか|av-masaka}鍵[かぎ]を家[いえ]に忘[わす]れたんじゃないだろうね。
en: Surely you didn't leave your keys at home, did you?
why: まさか introduces a doubtful 'don't tell me ...' guess about something unlikely.

jp: まさか兄[あに]が結婚[けっこん]する{とは/なんて|av-masaka}思[おも]わなかった。
en: I never imagined that my older brother would get married.
why: まさか is answered by とは思わなかった: 'I never thought that ...'.

jp: このジャムの瓶[びん]は、ふたが{なかなか|av-nakanaka}開[あ]きません。
en: The lid of this jam jar just won't come open.
why: なかなか + a negative means something does not happen easily, however hard you try.

jp: 妹[いもうと]の作[つく]ったカレーは{なかなか|av-nakanaka}おいしかった。
en: The curry my little sister made was quite good.
why: なかなか + a positive word is praise: 'rather good'.

jp: 今度[こんど]の休[やす]みには、{ぜひ|av-zehi}うちに遊[あそ]びに来[き]てください。
en: Please be sure to come and visit us during the next holiday.
why: ぜひ goes with a request (ください) or a wish.

jp: ぜひ祖父母[そふぼ]の家[いえ]に行[い]き{たいです|av-zehi}。
en: I really want to go to my grandparents' house.
why: ぜひ is paired with a wish such as たいです.

jp: {もし|av-moshi}明日[あした]雨[あめ]が降[ふ]ったら、洗濯物[せんたくもの]は部屋[へや]の中[なか]に干[ほ]します。
en: If it rains tomorrow, I will hang the laundry inside the room.
why: もし opens a hypothetical condition ending in たら.

jp: もし母[はは]が病気[びょうき]に{なったら/なれば|av-moshi}、すぐ帰[かえ]ります。
en: If my mother falls ill, I will go home at once.
why: もし sets up a supposition, so a conditional form is needed.

jp: {たとえ|av-tatoe}疲[つか]れていても、毎日[まいにち]子供[こども]に本[ほん]を読[よ]んであげます。
en: Even if I am tired, I read a book to my child every day.
why: たとえ opens a concessive clause ending in ても.

jp: いくら{呼[よ]んでも|av-tatoe}、弟[おとうと]は返事[へんじ]をしません。
en: No matter how often I call him, my brother doesn't answer.
why: いくら calls for the concessive ても form.

jp: 赤[あか]ちゃんの寝顔[ねがお]は{まるで|av-marude}天使[てんし]のようだ。
en: The baby's sleeping face is just like an angel's.
why: まるで pairs with のようだ in a vivid comparison.

jp: 母[はは]の部屋[へや]はまるでホテルの{ように/みたいに|av-marude}きれいだ。
en: My mother's room is as tidy as a hotel.
why: まるで is followed by ように or みたいに in a comparison.

jp: {どうやら/どうも|av-doumo}隣[となり]の家[いえ]は引[ひ]っ越[こ]したらしい。
en: Apparently the neighbours have moved out.
why: An inference from signs, closed by らしい, takes どうやら.

jp: 朝[あさ]から頭[あたま]が痛[いた]い。どうも風邪[かぜ]を{ひいたようだ|av-doumo}。
en: My head has hurt since this morning. It seems I have caught a cold.
why: どうも gives a vague impression and goes with ようだ.

jp: 今日[きょう]は{とても/かなり/ずいぶん|av-degree}忙[いそが]しくて、昼[ひる]ご飯[はん]を食[た]べる時間[じかん]もなかった。
en: I was so busy today that I didn't even have time for lunch.
why: A high degree with a positive predicate is とても.

jp: 姉[あね]は料理[りょうり]が{あまり|av-degree}得意[とくい]ではない。
en: My older sister is not very good at cooking.
why: あまり with a negative means 'not very'.

jp: 夕飯[ゆうはん]は{もう|av-mou-mada}食[た]べましたから、大丈夫[だいじょうぶ]です。
en: I have already eaten dinner, so I'm fine.
why: もう with a completed action means 'already'.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は{まだ|av-mou-mada}宿題[しゅくだい]が終[お]わっていません。
en: My little brother hasn't finished his homework yet.
why: まだ + ていません means 'not yet'.

jp: 夜[よる]の十時[じゅうじ]だ。{そろそろ|av-time}子供[こども]を寝[ね]かせよう。
en: It's ten at night. Let's put the kids to bed soon.
why: そろそろ means 'it's about time to' and fits a volitional ending.

jp: 洗濯機[せんたくき]が{さっき|av-time}止[と]まったので、洗濯物[せんたくもの]を干[ほ]しに行[い]きます。
en: The washing machine stopped a moment ago, so I'm going to hang the laundry.
why: さっき refers to a moment just past.

jp: 一時間[いちじかん]かかって、{やっと|av-time}部屋[へや]の掃除[そうじ]が終[お]わった。
en: After an hour, the cleaning of the room was finally done.
why: やっと expresses relief that something finally happened after effort.

jp: どんなに{忙[いそが]しくても|av-tatoe}、家族[かぞく]と夕飯[ゆうはん]を食[た]べます。
en: However busy I am, I eat dinner with my family.
why: どんなに asks for the concessive ても.

jp: 兄[あに]は掃除[そうじ]を全然[ぜんぜん]{しません|av-zenzen}。
en: My older brother doesn't clean at all.
why: 全然 demands a negative ending.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]は雨[あめ]の日[ひ]にはめったに外[そと]に{出[で]ません|av-mettani}。
en: My grandmother hardly ever goes out on rainy days.
why: めったに must end in a negative.

jp: 母[はは]はおそらく夕方[ゆうがた]には帰[かえ]って{くるでしょう|av-kitto}。
en: My mother will probably be back by evening.
why: おそらく is closed by a guess ending such as でしょう.

jp: まさか父[ちち]が約束[やくそく]を忘[わす]れることは{ないだろう|av-masaka}。
en: Surely my father won't forget his promise.
why: まさか is followed by ないだろう: 'surely not'.

jp: ぜひまた遊[あそ]びに来[き]て{ください|av-zehi}。
en: Please do come and see us again.
why: ぜひ goes with a request.

jp: 万一[まんいち]地震[じしん]が{起[お]きたら/起[お]きれば|av-moshi}、家族[かぞく]みんなで庭[にわ]に集[あつ]まります。
en: If an earthquake should happen, the whole family will gather in the garden.
why: 万一 opens a remote supposition and needs a conditional.

jp: 姉[あね]の部屋[へや]は{まるで|av-marude}倉庫[そうこ]のように物[もの]がいっぱいだ。
en: My sister's room is full of things, just like a warehouse.
why: まるで ... のように makes a comparison.

jp: せっかく家族[かぞく]が集[あつ]まった{のだから|av-sekkaku}、みんなで写真[しゃしん]を撮[と]りましょう。
en: Now that the whole family has gathered specially, let's take a photo together.
why: せっかく ... のだから gives a reason for making the most of the chance.

jp: 赤[あか]ちゃんが夜[よる]なかなか寝[ね]{てくれません|av-nakanaka}。
en: The baby won't go to sleep at night.
why: なかなか needs a negative ending: 'not easily'.

jp: 父[ちち]の帰[かえ]りは{ずいぶん/かなり/とても|av-degree}遅[おそ]かった。
en: My father came home quite late.
why: A strong degree in a positive sentence is ずいぶん.

jp: お風呂[ふろ]には{もう|av-mou-mada}入[はい]った？
en: Have you already taken your bath?
why: もう in a question asks whether it is already done.

jp: 弟[おとうと]は{たまに|av-time}夜中[よなか]に起[お]きて、冷蔵庫[れいぞうこ]を開[あ]けています。
en: My little brother sometimes wakes in the night and opens the fridge.
why: たまに means 'once in a while'.

jp: 明日[あした]の朝[あさ]は{たぶん/おそらく|av-kitto}雨[あめ]でしょう。
en: It will probably rain tomorrow morning.
why: たぶん goes with でしょう for a likely guess.

jp: 隣[となり]の犬[いぬ]が吠[ほ]えている。どうやら誰[だれ]かが{来[き]たらしい/来[き]たようだ|av-doumo}。
en: The neighbour's dog is barking. Apparently somebody has come.
why: どうやら is closed by らしい or ようだ.

jp: 子供[こども]は野菜[やさい]を{全然[ぜんぜん]/ちっとも|av-zenzen}食[た]べない。
en: My child doesn't eat vegetables at all.
why: A flat 'not at all' with a negative verb is 全然.

jp: 姉[あね]は{めったに|av-mettani}テレビを見[み]ません。
en: My older sister hardly ever watches TV.
why: めったに + a negative means 'rarely'.
